383YE Summer Solstice interlude.d: Military captains could Slow the Vallorn in Brocéliande, serve either side of the Asavean uprising, escort lost orcs to Skarsind, or join a Mission of Mercy into the Barrens. Fleets could join Dominate the Bay against the Grendel. The Guerdon of 175 Thrones went to four named armies. Trade was hit by Grendel piracy, sanctions on Asavea, turmoil in Axos, the closure of Robec and Jarmish tariffs, while the Commonwealth offered bonuses. Synod mandates, Tharim's feast on Navarr lands, Varushkan prosperity and the Wondrous Forests enchantment altered production, and Tithe of Bats entered Imperial Lore.

n.Dawn: Dawnish characters received extra rewards for helping Slow the Vallorn in Brocéliande, and captains could join a Mission of Mercy to rescue captured children of Dawn from the Barrens.
n.Druj: The Mission of Mercy opportunity offered Imperial captains a secretive foray into the Barrens to free captured children and other slaves and frustrate the Druj.
n.Grendel: Grendel pirates continued raiding Bay of Catazar shipping and pillaging Feroz, while Imperial fleets were offered a counterattack, Dominate the Bay, to challenge their dominance there.
n.Highguard: Highborn congregations lost two votes and one liao through the Blade of the Pilgrims fighting in Brocéliande, and Highborn fleets trading in the Bay suffered a rank penalty from Grendel piracy.
n.Imperial Orcs: Allies could escort lost orcs to Skarsind for a reward, funded by an Imperial Orc assembly mandate that imposed a one-rank penalty on every orc-owned farm, business, herb garden, forest, mine, mana site and fleet.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: any Lasambrian Jotun plunder after the Spring Equinox would have no effect on personal resources because protective magic persisted over Segura.
n.Navarr: Every Navarr herb garden lost two random herbs per season under the Blood and Gold mandate, and Tharim's feast reduced herb gardens and forests in Miaren, Therunin and Hercynia until the Winter Solstice 383YE.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast fleets suffered a rank penalty from Grendel pirates, and all personal resources in Feroz faced a two-rank penalty from Grendel pillaging, though Segura remained protected.
n.The League: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered a rank penalty from Grendel piracy, while congregations in Temeschwar and Tassato gained votes and liao under Rafael Barossa di Tassato's Reject False Gods mandate.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's Blood and Gold mandate supported Good Leaf Gardens in Upwold in recognition of the Marcher sacrifice fighting the vallorn of Liathaven.
n.Urizen: Urizen fleets trading in the Bay suffered a rank penalty from Grendel piracy, while congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod opposes idolatry.
n.Varushka: Varushkan mines and forests gained a rank of production, potentially for a year if Raskylov provided a suitable story, and Karsk congregations gained four extra votes and two liao for a year.
n.Wintermark: Congregations in Hahnmark gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate while the Synod maintains its anti-idolatry stance.

t.Bay of Catazar: Grendel pirates continued harassing shipping in the Bay, and Imperial fleets could join a damaging counterattack to challenge Grendel dominance there for a share of seized goods.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn continued to expand in Brocéliande; captains could help the steadings Slow the Vallorn, while Highborn congregations and the eternal Tharim also aided its defence.
t.Feroz: Every character based in Feroz faced a two-rank penalty to personal resource production from Grendel pillaging, though the Asavean temple there still boosted Imperial trade with Nemoria.
t.Hahnmark: Congregations in Hahnmark gained two votes and one liao after builders forcibly redesigned the Asavean-designed buildings there.
t.Hercynia: Tharim was permitted to feast on Hercynia's herb gardens and forests, each losing two herbs or resources until the Winter Solstice 383YE.
t.Karsk: Karsk congregations received four extra votes and two liao for a year under the Reject False Gods mandate, then the lesser bonus given elsewhere.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher sacrifice in fighting the vallorn of Liathaven was the reason Good Leaf Gardens were supported in Upwold.
t.Miaren: Herb gardens and forests in Miaren were fed upon by Tharim, losing two herbs or resources each until the Winter Solstice 383YE.
t.Redoubt: Congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao as the Asavean-designed buildings there were forcibly redesigned.
t.Sarvos: Fleets from Sarvos trading out of the Bay suffered a one-rank production penalty from Grendel pirate raids.
t.Segura: The magic that protected Segura from Corazón raids persisted, so any Lasambrian Jotun plunder would not affect personal resources there.
t.Skarsind: Lost orcs across the Empire sought to reach Skarsind, and Imperial captains could escort them there to safety.
t.Tassato: Tassato's fleets suffered a rank penalty from Grendel piracy, while its congregations gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate.
t.Temeschwar: Congregations in Temeschwar gained two votes and one liao after the Asavean-designed buildings there were forcibly redesigned.
t.Therunin: Therunin's herb gardens and forests lost two herbs or resources each to Tharim's feast until the Winter Solstice 383YE.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's Blood and Gold mandate was a consequence of supporting Good Leaf Gardens in Upwold.

383YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.d: All six eternals agreed to some form of parley with the archmages, and new opportunities opened at Anvil. The Sand Fishers left Bittershore for Misericorde in Holberg and began trading with the League. Brocéliande faced a building vallorn onslaught, while Westwood was liberated and a pristine weirwood forest found there. The Brass Coast, Navarr, the Marches, Varushka, Wintermark and several assemblies were each offered opportunities. The Basilica of Seven Doors was restored. Two miasma pillars were found in Ossium. Mobs stripped Almodin's commissions, and magistrates are now investigating. Vengeful Feni sacked the Singing Caves, and as many as fourteen wains of mithril are missing. Frederick di Sarvos threatened to leave the Empire.

n.Dawn: Dawn was named among those holding Brocéliande against the swelling vallorn, and its national assembly was invited to answer the grey pilgrims' questions. The Dawnish Cardinal of Ambition, Viviane de Coeurdefer, is tied to Frederick di Sarvos's stalled offer.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are listed as one of the Empire's orc neighbours. They once ruled the Sand Fishers and left behind the miasma still choking Ossium.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are listed as one of the four orc nations bordering the Empire, and orc slaves recently rescued from them are noted.
n.Highguard: The Basilica of Seven Doors in Bastion was restored and the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly reinstated. Highborn statements guide the grey pilgrims, and Highguard is also tagged in the Brocéliande defence and magical developments.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc assembly was tagged in the Sand Fishers' settlement of Holberg, the integration of the Mournwold thralls and wider orc affairs, where the many orc peoples are described as being in states ranging from war to uneasy truce with the Empire.
n.Jotun: Thralls the Jotun left behind in the Mournwold may be drawn into the Marcher nation. The Brass Coast offered a bounty to any Imperial who would fight the Lasambrian Jotun, and the Stormcrows declared Suaq who became Jotun thralls to be Frayed.
n.Navarr: The Navarr could raise a new vallorn-fighting army, with or without the Queen of Scorpions, and weighed three visions for Seren. They also held Brocéliande through another season and celebrated the vallorn's defeat in Liathaven.
n.The Brass Coast: Barbarians threaten every Brass Coast territory except Madruga. The Freeborn were offered a mithril exchange towards restoring the Burning Falcon, proposals to strengthen Segura, a salvage port, the Broken Shore Bounty and a bounty against the Lasambrian Jotun, and a Freeborn could become captain of the Passion of the Flame.
n.The League: League burghers gained a trade in herbs, delicacies and hides with the Sand Fishers in Holberg, and bishops proposed reinvigorating Capodomus Cathedral. Someone could also become leader of the Revelry, and a mandate under Rafael Barossa di Tassato sent mobs against Almodin's works.
n.The Marches: The Marcher assembly and the Senate examined bringing the Mournwold thralls into the Marcher nation. Feni sacked the Singing Caves, leaving Abbot Thomas Arch only seven wains of mithril, and Abbot Matilda of Becktunn championed Marcher common sense and a lost exemplar of Ambition.
n.Thule: Thule forces are currently the only defenders of Ossium, and few of the territory's people have any reason to trust them. An Ambassador to Otkodov is among those concerned with orc affairs.
n.Varushka: The Varushkans could raise a memorial to the paragon Zoria with true liao, and wise ones weighed the role of the Tender of the Hearth. In newly conquered Ossium, two miasma pillars were found, but defence and the many resident orcs remain pressing problems.
n.Wintermark: The Stormcrows' celebration of heroism opened opportunities for a daring raid, a mystical rookery and a chronicle of heroes. Their declaring Jotun-thralled Suaq Frayed provoked a very different reaction, and the Crows highlighted the parlous state of the Hall of Rund.

t.Bastion: The Senate-commissioned refurbishment of the Basilica of Seven Doors was quickly completed with the Custodes Clavium's help, and the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly was reinstated.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn's attacks have grown for nine months and are expected to crest next season. If the Empire holds for three more months the threat should end for now, possibly with new opportunity.
t.Holberg: The Sand Fishers settled Misericorde as recognised foreigners, founding villages and trading rare goods with League citizens. They shun the city itself and the bandit-haunted woods of Utterlund.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold Marchers are said to have more in common with the Jotun thralls than with people across the border in Kahraman.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is not named on the page. The Varushkan matters discussed are Zoria's claimed resting place in the Vale of Gniejezdo and the situation in Ossium.
t.Liathaven: Imperial forces won a decisive victory over the vallorn, claiming Westwood and an unlooked-for pristine weirwood forest ripe for development.
t.Madruga: Madruga is the only Brass Coast territory not threatened by barbarians, and there is an opportunity to build a salvage port there.
t.Mournwold: Marchers and Jotun thralls who stayed behind have become neighbours after thirty years of shared labour. Both the Senate and the Marcher assembly sought their integration, and Feni raided the Singing Caves in the Ore Hills.
t.Ossium: Ser Ancél Watcher's work uncovered the first two miasma pillars, likely one per region. The territory is defended only by the distrusted Thule and holds many orcs less tractable than the Sand Fishers.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov is tagged as having an interest in the season's orc affairs.
t.Segura: The Senate signalled it would not abandon Segura to the western invaders, and the architect Angelina i Duarte i Riqueza put forward proposals to strengthen it.
t.Sermersuaq: The Stormcrows declared the Suaq who became Jotun thralls to be Frayed, a judgement that has provoked a strong reaction among the people of Sermersuaq.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral itself is not discussed. The nearest reference is the Spiral Sword runeforge, one of Almodin's works stripped by mobs.
t.Tassato: League citizens, especially those of Tassato, are flagged as concerned by the season's magical developments. Rafael Barossa di Tassato enacted the mandate that sent mobs against Almodin's works.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers crossed the Semmerlak from Bittershore to reach their new home in Misericorde.
t.Upwold: Nearly a gross of Feni gathered in a copse near the Old Pig before splitting. Those heading northeast into the Silver Chase were quickly dealt with by Marcher heroes arriving through the Sentinel Gate.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Boar's Dell is one of the footholds of civilisation threatened by a coming tidal wave of vallorn malice that must be endured for one more season.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Elerael is one of the footholds of civilisation threatened by a coming tidal wave of vallorn malice that must be endured for one more season.
r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Sand Fishers prefer roaming the marshes of Ennerlund to visiting the city of Holberg.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Ceded to the Sand Fishers, Misericorde quickly gained small orc villages that exploit its abundant wildlife.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: The Sand Fishers range into the marshes of Rebeshof rather than the city of Holberg.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: The Sand Fishers are wary of Utterlund's deep woods, fearing the bandits there and perhaps reminded of the Druj.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Imperial forces drove the vallorn out of Westwood, claiming the region and discovering a pristine weirwood forest.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Vengeful Feni crossed the Ore Hills to sack the Singing Caves. They slaughtered miners and left as many as fourteen wains of mithril missing, though the mine should return to full production next season.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: The Sand Fishers abandoned Bittershore with civil service help and crossed the Semmerlak to settle Misericorde.

383YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: Two Highborn armies narrowly held Segura against the Lasambrian Jotun. In Feroz, Marcher and Navarr armies were pushed back and Bramar fell, leaving the Grendel nine-tenths of the way to taking the territory. The vallorn was held in Brocéliande, though it is expected to crest next season. League armies destroyed Llofir's Castle of Ruin, and Tamarbode was restored without its Spring regio. Imperial and Axou captains sank hundreds of Grendel ships and raided Gainmeachdubh. The Jotun took two-thirds of Serra Damata. The Druj threw back the Barrens invasion and executed prisoners, but the Mission of Mercy freed the Drycastle children and many slaves. Six armies cleansed Westwood, confining Liathaven's vallorn to Liath's Heart. Five Sentinel Gate conjunctions were identified.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Hounds of Glory, Eastern Sky, Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride invaded Dawnguard and were driven back to Semmerholm with nearly a thousand dead, after which the Druj executed hundreds of Dawnish prisoners. The Mission of Mercy freed the Drycastle children and about two-fifths of the missing Dawnish citizens.
n.Druj: The Druj, prepared with traps, Spring and Night magic and the White Lion's coordination, repelled the invasion of Dawnguard and slaughtered prisoners in reprisal. They nonetheless lost the Drycastle children and many slaves to the Mission of Mercy, while their forces in Spiral fell quiet.
n.Grendel: The Grendel armada took Bramar and nearly all of Fontargenta, holding Feroz's coast and ilium offices. At sea, however, hundreds of their ships were sunk or crippled, Gainmeachdubh was raided, and their supply convoys will struggle to resupply for a year.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar and Seventh Wave held Segura at a cost of some fifteen hundred Highborn. Highguard's Remember Exile garrison was key to liberating Tamarbode, Highborn ships sank many Grendel supply convoys, and Highborn priests and a national mandate aided Brocéliande.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm fought in the Westwood, where one of its patrols found an untouched weirwood grove, while orc defenders repelled Jotun raiders in Skarsind. Imperial Orc captains also joined raids on Grendel ports, though they were absent from the Mission of Mercy.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun failed to advance in Segura but kept Anduzjasse, while the Bear-Who-Swims and Skjalderborn took two-thirds of Serra Damata. The Jotun still hold all of Sermersuaq except Sealtoq and four regions of Liathaven.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns led the cleansing of the Westwood, confining the Liathaven vallorn to Liath's Heart, and the vallorn was held in Brocéliande with many allies. The Quiet Step harried the Grendel in Feroz, while Tharim continues to feed on Navarr forests and herb gardens.
n.The Brass Coast: Three of the four Freeborn territories are now invaded: Segura narrowly held, Feroz nearly lost to the Grendel, and Serra Damata in Kahraman two-thirds taken by the Jotun. Freeborn corsairs were prominent in the campaign that broke Grendel control of the Bay.
n.The League: The Towerjacks and Wolves of War, with Holberg siege engineers, stormed the Castle of Ruin and liberated Tamarbode. League captains hunted Grendel pirates in the Bay, and League citizens captured in Holberg years ago were freed from the Druj.
n.The Marches: The Strong Reeds and Bounders fought the Grendel in Feroz but were forced to abandon Bramar. The Drakes helped cleanse the Westwood of Liathaven.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard defended Elerael in Brocéliande and studied the vallorn's magic, and Urizen ships sank many Grendel supply convoys. Around a hundred Urizen captives taken from Zenith were freed from Druj slavery.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe joined the failed invasion of Dawnguard, liberating smaller settlements before the retreat, and captured Varushkan soldiers were among those executed by the Druj. Varushkan ships preyed on Grendel merchant vessels.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks and Fist of the Mountains left Sermersuaq to help cleanse the Westwood, while the Beacons of Wintermark turned back Jotun raiders in Kallavesa and Hahnmark. Wintermark has by far the largest force weight for the Solstice conjunctions.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: its noble houses and villages support Dawnish champions in Brocéliande, and many Astolat citizens are listed among those taking part.
t.Ayereed: Ayereed suffered lightning raids by Imperial captains culminating in the attack on Gainmeachdubh, contributing to a bounty of mithril and ilium.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion captains are listed among those who sailed against the Grendel.
t.Bay of Catazar: Imperial and Axou captains sank or crippled hundreds of Grendel ships, ending the Grendel hunt of Imperial traders and halving their resupply for a year. They were not strong enough to disrupt the Rites of Spring, however.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the armies bound for Liathaven marched through its marshes, and Bregasland captains are listed in the naval campaign.
t.Brocéliande: Defenders held back the vallorn for a third season with the Citadel Guard, Great Forest orcs and other allies, but their reserves are taxed and the vallorn's wave has yet to crest.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea citizens are listed among those aiding Brocéliande and the naval campaign.
t.Feroz: The Grendel now hold Oranseri and the Cazar Straits and nine-tenths of Fontargenta after taking Bramar, along with the ilium offices and the Temple of Balo. Over fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers were lost, and residents continue to suffer raids.
t.Hahnmark: Jotun raiders from Sermersuaq met stiff resistance at the lit Beacons of Wintermark and were turned back.
t.Hercynia: Tharim continues to feast on Hercynia's forests and herb gardens, costing each a rank of production for a year in return for his aid in Brocéliande.
t.Holberg: The armies bound for the Barrens passed through Holberg, its university supplied siege engineers for Tamarbode, and masked boatmen carried liberators and freed children along the river.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the Bear-That-Swims earlier crossed from Hordalant to attack West Ranging.
t.Kahraman: The Jotun invaded again from the west and took two-thirds of Serra Damata, held back from Damata and the white granite cliffs only by the Fort Braydon garrison.
t.Kallavesa: Jotun raiders were repelled at the borders, and the armies bound for Liathaven marched through Kallavesa's marshes.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov citizens are listed among the captains who sailed against the Grendel.
t.Liathaven: Six Imperial armies cleansed the Westwood, leaving the vallorn confined to Liath's Heart, at a cost of over three thousand lives. The Jotun still hold the territory, and the Paths of Lan Thúven are gone.
t.Madruga: With the Grendel holding the southern ends of the Scorrero bridges, armies can no longer enter Feroz from Madruga without fighting. A few Freeborn refugees are being smuggled there.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: earlier Imperial raids on Mareave and Beoraidh are said to have enraged the Salt Lords.
t.Miaren: Tharim continues to feed on Miaren's forests and herb gardens, costing each a rank of production for a year.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova citizens are listed in the naval campaign and the Mission of Mercy.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: a Mitwold captain is listed in the naval campaign.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard came to Brocéliande fresh from fighting the Druj in Morrow, bringing husks raised from the fallen there.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders came to Feroz from furlough in the Mournwold, which Fort Braydon overlooks.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis citizens are listed among the captains who sailed against the Grendel.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: with the fighting in Ossium over for now, the five armies that conquered it marched south to invade the Barrens.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt citizens are listed among those aiding Brocéliande and the naval campaign.
t.Reikos: Tamarbode was liberated, Llofir vanished and the region was restored as forest, though its Spring regio and Tamar's Toes were destroyed.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: some Freeborn refugees are smuggled out of Feroz to Sarvos, and ships sailed from its docks to hunt the Grendel.
t.Segura: Highborn armies narrowly held the line against the Lasambrian Jotun at a cost of some fifteen hundred dead. The protective Autumn magic is fading, seven Towers of Anduz remain in orc hands, and destitute refugees strain the eastern towns.
t.Semmerholm: The armies gathered at Axmure before invading the Barrens and retreated there in defeat, and the Druj raised a field of heads on spikes in sight of its forests. Semmerholm yeofolk also guided liberators into Dawnguard.
t.Sermersuaq: The Jotun rule all of Sermersuaq except Sealtoq, which they are keeping their oath not to enter for a year. Their raids south and east are being repelled.
t.Shayeel: Imperial captains made lightning raids on Grendel pirate settlements in Shayeel, contributing to a bounty of 12 wains of mithril and 6 rings of ilium.
t.Skarsind: Jotun raiders from Sermersuaq crossed into Skarsind and clashed with its Imperial Orc defenders.
t.Spiral: There has been no news of Druj movements since they took Ossuary and Screed, and it is unclear whether any major Druj force remains. Roughly a third of Spiral is still under their nominal control.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the gentler route through Tassato into Feroz is closed to Marcher armies while the Grendel hold Oranseri.
t.Tathar: Mentioned in passing: Grendel trade ships avoid the channel between the Iron Confederacy and Tathar.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar citizens are listed in the naval campaign and the Mission of Mercy.
t.The Barrens: The Dawnish-Varushkan invasion of Dawnguard was repelled and prisoners were executed in reprisal, but the Mission of Mercy freed the Drycastle children, many slaves and 10 wains of weirwood. Freed slaves report that the Towers of Dusk have been rebuilt as a great citadel.
t.Therunin: Tharim continues to feed on Therunin's forests and herb gardens. A thousand freed orcs and three hundred orc children joined the Great Forest orcs here, with liberators and Navarr scouts using it as a route into the Barrens.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: an Upwold captain is listed in the naval campaign.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: a Volodmartz captain is listed in the naval campaign.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: many Weirwater citizens are listed among those aiding Brocéliande and the Mission of Mercy.
t.Zenith: Around a hundred Urizen citizens taken north from Zenith were found enslaved in Peytaht and the Carmine Fields and were freed.

r.Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh: Imperial captains raided this prosperous Grendel port under the gaze of Salt Lord Azshur, damaging the harbour and burning over two dozen pirate ships at anchor.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: Mentioned in passing: a captain 'of North Fens' is listed in the naval campaign.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Boar's Dell was defended against the vallorn's push, helped by the destruction of the North Weaver Wood herald. Great Forest orcs born here returned to fight for it.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: The Citadel Guard and their husks stood ready to defend Elerael, freeing other defenders to concentrate on Boar's Dell.
r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the vallorn of Brocéliande is described pressing outward into Boar's Dell and Elerael.
r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Imperial troops remain billeted near Afar and the borders of Afarjasse, and Grendel looters raided Afar. The armada cannot push inland here without land forces.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Grendel have uncontested control of the region, including Cazar and its ilium office, halting ilium collection.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Bramar fell after a three-day stand and was looted, leaving the Grendel nine-tenths of the way to taking the region and with it the territory.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The nearly finished Mora's Rock served as the Imperial base of operations, and Grendel looters raided Mora. The Bounders arrived here via the Cinnabar Hills.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Grendel hold Oranseri and the southern ends of the Scorrero bridges, and the Strong Reeds' push here was driven back. The Scorrero Bluffs are a Sentinel Gate conjunction for the Solstice.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: the armies marched through the woods of northern Holberg, where poisonous plants no longer grow.
r.Holberg/The Morass: Mentioned in passing: the armies trudged through the stinking mud of the Morass on their way south.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Mentioned in passing: the armies passed through its woods, now free of the poisonous plants that once grew there.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Fort Braydon garrison slowed the Jotun, but many of its soldiers are in precarious positions as the Solstice nears.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named and is touched only by the wider Jotun invasion of Kahraman.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Dhomiro of Serra Briante sent warriors west to resist, and Jotun raiders pushed toward Rojota. The Rojota Road is a Sentinel Gate conjunction for the Solstice.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Jotun overran two-thirds of Serra Damata, but defenders held Damata and its white granite cliffs.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: The vallorn of Liathaven is now confined to Liath's Heart around the ruined Terunael city, and it is more dangerous than ever.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The Jotun had withdrawn, so West Ranging stayed Imperial and carried the supply lines for the Westwood campaign. It can now be reached on foot from Western Scout.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: It is now possible to walk from Western Scout to West Ranging. Fallen Thorn Stead, a Jotun meeting point here, is a Sentinel Gate conjunction.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Westwood was cleansed of the vallorn and conquered by the Empire, and a healthy weirwood grove was found here. The Heartway is a Sentinel Gate conjunction for the Solstice.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: the earlier Imperial raid on Beoraidh is recalled, and Gainmeachdubh is compared to it in size.
r.Reikos/Broken Ride: The garrison of Remember Exile, the fortification here, was a major factor in liberating Tamarbode.
r.Reikos/Grey Charge: Mentioned in passing: the League armies gathered beneath its boughs, hosted by its chapters, before entering Tamarbode.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: Mentioned in passing: veterans recall the horror of its liberation when facing Druj traps in Dawnguard.
r.Reikos/Longshire: Mentioned in passing: the League armies gathered here as guests of its rebuilt chapterhouses.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Tamarbode was liberated and is now forested and Springtouched. Its Spring regio and Tamar's Toes are gone, and the Sign of Tamar is being reclaimed by the forest.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Anduzjasse remains wholly in Lasambrian Jotun hands, and refugees continue to flee east from it.
r.Segura/Anozeseri: The Jotun foothold in Anozeseri was neither expanded nor reduced. Losing any of its Towers of Anduz would end the great work's benefits.
r.Segura/Burnish: If the orcs take any Towers of Anduz in Burnish, the great work's entire benefit will be lost.
r.Segura/Iron Plains: A force of Escuta led by a pale-skinned shaman shadowed Granite Pillar troops escorting refugees across the Iron Plains, the site of an old slaughter, but largely avoided battle.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: Its Towers of Anduz are at risk should the orcs advance. The Ambergris Valley here is a Sentinel Gate conjunction for the Solstice.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: The invading armies regrouped in Axmure, and the Druj raised a forest of spiked heads in sight of its forests.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Sealtoq is the only region not held by the Jotun, whose rulers are keeping their oath not to march into it for a year.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Druj push into Apulus was halted last season, and no further Druj movement has been reported.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Ossuary and the Legacy remain under Druj control, though no further activity has been seen.
r.Spiral/Screed: Screed and the Black Plateau remain under Druj control after their rites there, though no Druj movements are reported.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: The invasion of Dawnguard was driven back and the Druj executed hundreds of prisoners, but the Drycastle children and many slaves were freed.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: Mentioned in passing: savage beasts from Farweald followed the Druj into Dawnguard.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Heroes struck slave camps here, freeing Urizen captives working the weirwood forest, and some freed children escaped through Peytaht to Reikos.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Three hundred freed orc children were brought to the sanctuary at Hope's Rest before being taken on to Therunin.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Heroes of the Mission of Mercy struck against slave camps in Murderdale.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Malignant marsh creatures from Saltmarsh harried Imperial soldiers, and orc children taken from Saltmarsh were among those rescued.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: Mentioned in passing: savage beasts out of the Bleaks fought in the Druj's wake in Dawnguard.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: Orc children were rescued from the Plains of Teeth, and freed slaves report thriving Druj towns there.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Most of the freed Drycastle children reached freedom by travelling south through the Lower Tarn Valley.

A dream that can last.d: After abandoning Ossium and crossing the Semmerlak, the Sand Fishers built simple villages in Misericorde and roamed Holberg's marshes. Their wanderings onto farmland were settled by agreement: in return for access they tithe herbs, so every Holberg farm now yields two random herbs each season. Cultural friction, including an incident at the Imperial Menagerie, led to calls for a market outside the city. Tristan Exile's End used an Imperial Wayleave to commission Misericorde Market. The Synod sent Kaspar Yakovitch von Holberg to teach the Virtues, Leonora Van Holberg to rally Holberg's citizens, and Skywise Rykana to rally the Imperial Orcs. Each mandate carried costs for those it called upon.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the Sand Fishers' former enslavers, whose miasma crushed their spirit, and as the one-time masters of Ossium's forests.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc assembly sent Skywise Rykana to rally support for the Sand Fishers. Under the mandate, Imperial Orc-owned resources were to produce one rank less from the Summer Solstice until the Winter Solstice 383YE, with the Sand Fishers gaining what the orcs gave up.
n.The League: Holberg's citizens gained herb tithes on their farms and a new market for Sand Fisher goods. In return, Leonora Van Holberg's mandate called on them to support their new neighbours at a cost to Holberg's production, and Kaspar Yakovitch von Holberg was sent to teach the Sand Fishers the Virtues.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named directly, but the Sand Fishers' departure took place from Ossium, which Varushka held.

t.Holberg: The Sand Fishers settled in Misericorde and roam its marshes. Every farm in Holberg now gains two random herbs each season, Misericorde Market was commissioned beside the city, and a passed mandate called on Holberg's citizens to support the orcs at a temporary cost to production.
t.Ossium: With the civil service's help, the Sand Fishers abandoned Ossium and crossed the Semmerlak to their new home in Misericorde.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: a statement by the preachers of Skarsind urging Imperial Orcs to engage with the Sand Fishers is quoted, and the orcs' development of Skarsind is cited as an example.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Sand Fishers range into Ennerlund's marshes hunting and gathering herbs, and they tithe a share of the herbs they find to the owners of the farmland they cross.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers completed their claim on Misericorde and built small reed-and-wood villages near the Semmerlak. A covered market, Misericorde Market, was commissioned for trade between them and Holberg's citizens.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Sand Fishers wander Rebeshof's marshes in search of herbs, and they share a portion of their finds with local landowners in exchange for passage across their farms.

After the gold rush.d: Steinr thane Cenred Xunhand, inspired by Alfmund Forwinsson's Synod judgement, planned to offer a prize to the scop who told the best story of non-martial heroism; his Suaq daughter Erna died defending Skarsind. Vulpius, herald of Ephisis, was to hold a silent auction of curios in the Hall of Worlds. Something that arrived after the surge of Night magic invited visitors to a chamber beyond a night regio in Miaren, offering rewards for new experiences. Marquis Joueur was to auction an invitation to Prospero's Threadweaver game. Alejandro i Galiano i Erigo's ship, the Passion of Flame, was to be sold on the Bourse. The Revelry, former bandits of Holberg, sent Finn von Holberg to seek a new patron.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Cenred's daughter Erna is said to have died defending Skarsind, the Imperial Orc territory, alongside Britta of the Green Shields.
n.Navarr: An unknown entity has settled beyond a night regio used by local vates in Miaren, inviting people to perform for it and bring it new experiences in return for rewards.
n.The Brass Coast: A Galiano dhomiro, sickened by the slavery seen in Maragladia, was retiring to farm olives and putting their weirwood-reinforced ship up for sale, while Marquis Joueur intended to hold his auction at the Brass Coast camp.
n.The League: The Revelry, a Holberg military unit of former bandits, was seeking a new patron among Holberg-based guilds and free companies, with its quartermaster planning to report to a League egregore.
n.Wintermark: Thane Cenred Xunhand challenged the scops of Wintermark to tell the best tale of heroism that does not involve battle, offering a prize in the spirit of Alfmund Forwinsson's Synod judgement.

t.Holberg: The Revelry, awarded as spoils after Holberg's liberation in 379YE, had fallen on hard times guarding caravans and hunting bandits, and sought a new patron from Holberg's guilds and free companies.
t.Madruga: The Passion of Flame, a swift fleet based in the town of Calvos, was offered for sale on the Bourse as its owner retired from trade.
t.Miaren: Since the recent surge of Night magic, something new has made its home in a chamber beyond a night regio in a forest near the ruins of Seren, sending tendrils to invite visitors.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Erna, daughter of Cenred Xunhand, was killed defending Skarsind as adjutant of the Green Shields.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Revelry had been operating in the forests of Misericorde, fighting the bandits still infesting the woods, but found the work too poorly paid to continue without a patron.

Between the lines of ages.d: Irra Harah agreed to send a herald for a second parley with the Spring archmage on Friday at eight. Sinokenon, saying nothing had changed, will still send a mandarin to hear the Day archmage and invited cardinals at ten. The Lictors accepted a formal parley at eleven, with three questions and three answers. Rhianos's heralds will hear tales of adventure, especially against the Grendel, on Saturday at two. A gloomy Sadogua, mourning Richard of Holberg, will attend at half past eight and asked for a named group to gather by nine for a task. Skathe will meet the Winter archmage and the Wisest Senator about Zephaniah's Lament on Saturday at eleven, but only if the Conclave first grants her amity.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Ser Fabienne De Miel, Archmage of Spring, secured a second parley with Irra Harah's herald, and Sadogua asked for the most glorious witch-adept of Night lore in Dawn to join his gathering.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Irra Harah is credited with helping to free prisoners held by the Druj in the Barrens.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Rhianos helped the Empire secure the chance to attack the Grendel stronghold of Beoraidh, and wants to hear tales of the Empire's ventures against the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Brother Luke of the Shattered Tower, Archmage of Summer, will host Rhianos's heralds, who expect him to gather storytellers with tales of daring adventure.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skywise Gralka, Archmage of Day, secured a formal parley with Sinokenon's mandarin alongside Synod cardinals, while Sadogua sought a representative of the Circle of Zulgan Tash, and Irra Harah was credited with resettling orcs freed from Dubhtraig.
n.Navarr: Navarr's Syn Truth-Walker Returned, Archmage of Winter, was invited with the Wisest Senator to meet Skathe about Zephaniah's Lament, provided the Conclave grants her amity first.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's gloomy mood stems from the recent death of his long-time friend Richard of Holberg, the magical architect.
n.Urizen: Two Urizen archmages secured meetings: Edmundo of Damakan's Forge a formal parley with the Lictors, and Elyssiathain a parley with Sadogua, who asked for help gathering a special group.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua named Sovica of Varushka, or someone she appoints, among those he wants gathered for a task.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the death of the magical architect Richard of Holberg is the reason given for Sadogua's dark mood.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Irra Harah is credited with helping bring the lost orcs liberated from Dubhtraig to new homes in Skarsind.

Birds.d: Much of Zoria's story was lost when Nicovar burned the great libraries. At the Spring Equinox, the Varushka and Wisdom Assemblies recognised her maze in Gniejezdo as her original shrine. The maze, whose most recent guardian Domagoj Gnietzen vanished over two years ago, had languished. A rival site, a cave beneath Black Hill in the Opascari mountains, was looted by Thule raiders over a century ago. A shrine would cost 18 wains of white granite and 36 crowns at the maze. Its guardian would gain 9 liao and 18 Synod votes and might collect tales of Zoria. The Senate commissioned the shrine at the maze.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Starac Sijed, the maze's former guardian, gave up that charge when he and his family left Varushka for Dawn.
n.Thule: A Thule raiding party attacked and looted Zoria's Cave over a century ago, carrying off whatever was kept there. No one has ever been able to ask them what they took.
n.Varushka: Varushka gains a renewed focus on its patron of wise ones, with the Senate commissioning a shrine at Zoria's Maze. Its guardian might be elected by the Varushkan National Assembly and could gather the vales' scattered tales of her.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the stone tablet at the heart of Zoria's Cave is carved with hundreds of Wintermark runes.

t.Miekarova: The neglected maze in the Vale of Gniejezdo, Miekarova, was chosen as the site of the new shrine to Zoria. Its nearby chapel was to be greatly enlarged to welcome pilgrims.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Imperial scouts found the territory guarded by a twisting maze known locally as the Maze of Zora, almost certainly unconnected to Zoria.

Broken arrow.d: Henriika Ikkasbane devised a stealthy raid across Atkonaroq into Suaq Fount to strike the Pride of Ikka's Tears, recover mithril and free Suaq thralls. The raid would liberate 50 thralls per thousand strength committed, and Jotun patrols would then prevent further raids. The Assembly named Raknar Ravenstorm, Eyes of the North, to lead it, and Kindra Edasdottir sent half the Fist of the Mountains. The page does not record the raid's result. The Senate voted to rebuild the Ishal aviary, creating the Raven Seer title, and to create the Chronicle of Heroism. A controversial judgement declared Suaq thralls Frayed. Usko Argonning raised a follow-up mandate but withdrew it without it being enacted.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Wintermark statement praises Aethelric the Grounded's work at the field hospital in Zenith, without naming the Druj.
n.Jotun: Their Pride of Ikka's Tears mine and the halls of their jarls in Sermersuaq became the target of a Wintermark raid to free Suaq thralls and recover mithril. Wintermark statements also set their notion of honour apart from Wintermark heroism.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: most Wintermarkers are said to reject the brutal tactics of the Navarr as unheroic.
n.Wintermark: The Assembly named Raknar Ravenstorm to lead the raid, the Fist of the Mountains committed half its warriors, and the Senate commissioned the Ishal aviary and a Chronicle of Heroism for the nation. A judgement declaring thralls Frayed stirred controversy among stormcrows.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: freed Suaq thralls and recovered wealth were to be escorted back to Hahnmark and Kallavesa.
t.Kallavesa: The Senate voted to rebuild the aviary at Ishal, which would create the Raven Seer title for a Kallavesi-backed mystic. The territory was also to receive freed thralls.
t.Sermersuaq: Wintermark raiders struck at the Jotun-held lands to free Suaq thralls and reach Ikka's Tears, after which the Jotun were certain to tighten their patrols. The Assembly's judgement declaring those who took the choice to be Frayed caused controversy among Wintermarkers.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Aethelric the Grounded is praised for saving hundreds of lives at a field hospital in Zenith.

r.Kallavesa/Skymark: Ishal, in southern Skymark, was chosen as the site of the Senate-commissioned aviary, where mystics would read omens for the Raven Seer through the Parliament of Owls ritual.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The raid crossed Atkonaroq into Suaq Fount to reach the Pride of Ikka's Tears. A large enough force could have blocked the mine and prepared the region for an Imperial assault without the usual beachhead penalty.

Comes a time.d: Corey Wayfarer's greater-majority judgement urged a third Navarr army to fight the vallorn. The eternal Arhallogen offered to train it at a hall in Brocéliande, in exchange for Conclave amity or a precise declaration of concord, giving it the Silent Hunters quality. Critics instead proposed a costlier Thornbound army trained through Navarr herb lore and Spring magic. Enis's judgement on Seren inspired three mutually exclusive proposals: the Gardens of the Heart, the Temple of Waking Dream and the great library Isaella's Legacy. The Navarr raised Isaella's Dance with the Thornbound quality. The redesigned temple was completed in Autumn 388YE, creating the dreamspeaker archetype and a new title.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is named among the Empire's cities, Highborn cathedrals are a yardstick for the temple, and the Highborn's destruction of Llofir's fortress in Reikos is cited as a reason for Conclave caution.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Gildenheim in Skarsind is named among the recognised cities of the Empire.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the weakening of the vallorn in Liathaven, which the Jotun now hold, is cited as a sign that the vallorn can be beaten.
n.Navarr: The nation faced a choice between accepting Arhallogen's help or training its own vallorn-fighting army, and between three wonders for Seren. It raised the Thornbound army Isaella's Dance and later built the Temple of Waking Dream, which gave rise to the dreamspeaker archetype.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the Empire's recognised cities.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Meade is held up as the city Seren equals, and Marcher monetary wealth is contrasted with the Navarr's.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is named among the Empire's cities, the scop Topi appears in the opening tale, and the Wintermark Fight with honour order would affect both new army orders.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is named as one of the cities people think of before Seren.
t.Brocéliande: Arhallogen offered to raise a training hall for the new Navarr army around a regio in Brocéliande, needing no materials or Senate commission, if the Conclave approved. Some hope the territory's vallorn might be weakened if it can be withstood long enough.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is listed among the Empire's recognised cities.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Great Library of Hacynian is cited as an example of Navarr scholarship.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the weakening of Liathaven's vallorn is cited as encouragement for a dedicated vallorn-fighting army.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is named among the Empire's recognised cities.
t.Miaren: Seren in Miaren became the focus of three proposed great commissions meant to make it the Garden City, the City of Dreams or the City of Leaves. The Temple of Waking Dream was built, and every congregation in Miaren now receives an extra dose of liao and Goosewhisper Infusion each season.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Meade is named as the city Seren is said to equal.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn's forced destruction of Llofir's fortress in Reikos is cited as a reason the Conclave might refuse an eternal's commission.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Gildenheim is named among the Empire's cities and as the place where the scop Topi carried his books.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: it is one of the Navarr territories through which the Assembly's judgements were spread.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Boar's Dell was named as a likely site for Arhallogen's proposed training hall for the new Navarr army.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Elerael was named as a likely site for Arhallogen's proposed training hall for the new Navarr army.
r.Miaren/Serenael: Serenael was the site of the redesigned Temple of Waking Dream, completed in Autumn 388YE, which established the dreamspeaker archetype and a new Navarr title.

Construct Celestial Library at Canterspi.d: Proposed by Redoubt and seconded by Tassato, the commission came from an agreement between the people of Urizen and Phaleron, following proposals from the library's archivists. It aimed to secure the library in perpetuity against harm or invasion. The civil service set non-standard costs after talking with Novus, herald of Phaleron: 40 wains of mithril, 80 crowns and three months of work. After the Summer Solstice 383YE, Spyridonakes provided 10 thrones. Marcus gave 20 wains of mithril, and Thalia and Edmundo of Damakan's forge gave 10 wains each, covering the mithril required. When construction is complete, Canterspire will be ceded to Phaleron.

n.Urizen: Urizen gains the institution of Urizen Lore, a lasting monument to its magical Ambition and Pride, in return for giving up the Grand Library of Canterspire to the eternal Phaleron.

t.Morrow: The Grand Library of Canterspire is to be transformed and, once the work is complete, ceded to Phaleron so that it is protected in perpetuity against harm or invasion.

Construct House of Guerra.d: Proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by Kahraman, the motion commissioned a great work in Madruga to take advantage of a special opportunity, linked to supporting refugees, to construct a ministry for purchasing liao. It used non-standard costs of 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns of labour, was self-funded, and takes three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 383YE, Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra provided 5 thrones and 20 wains of white granite. On completion it will create the Hand of Guerra, a Freeborn national title appointed yearly by the Brass Coast National Assembly and revocable by the National and General Assemblies.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gain a new national position, the Hand of Guerra, appointed yearly by their National Assembly, and Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra personally supplied the white granite and funds for the work.

t.Madruga: Madruga is the site of the new House of Guerra, a ministry through which liao can be purchased, proposed by Madruga's own senator.

Construct Imperial Cord Brokerage II.d: Proposed by the senator for Miaren and seconded by Karov, the motion commissioned a ministry drawing on an opportunity presented by the broker of Navarr. It used non-standard costs of 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 383YE, Llewellyn Leafstalker provided 3 thrones, 7 crowns, 19 rings and the 16 wains of weirwood, with a further ring in small donations. On completion the brokerage would create a new Imperial title, the Broker of the Invisible Cord, appointed through the Bourse by Navarr owners of herb gardens.

n.Navarr: The ministry grew from an opportunity presented by the broker of Navarr, and its new title, the Broker of the Invisible Cord, would be chosen by Navarr owners of herb gardens through the Bourse.

t.Miaren: Miaren's senator proposed the motion, and the Invisible Cord Brokerage was to be built in Seren, Miaren, to guarantee prices for independent weirwood traders.

Construct Iron Qanat II.d: Proposed by Segura's senator and seconded by Sarvos, the motion set non-standard costs of 50 wains of weirwood and 100 crowns, with no upkeep and three months to build. It was self-funded: Alexios i Zemress i Riqueza provided the weirwood and crowns after the Summer Solstice. Although the motion named Yellow Chase, the Iron Qanat was built in the Sobral Grasses, as the Zemress islanders who provided the opportunity had proposed. The basic Iron Qanat allows the Brass Coast to support an additional army or navy, and the Red Plains Farm and the Golden Terraces would immediately be upgraded by a level if in Imperial hands.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained the capacity to support an additional army or navy and better supply for their existing forces, funded by Alexios i Zemress i Riqueza.

t.Segura: Segura's senator proposed the great work, which was built in the territory and would upgrade the Red Plains Farm and the Golden Terraces by a level if they were in Imperial hands.

r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The Iron Qanat was ultimately built in the Sobral Grasses, as proposed by the Zemress islanders who provided the opportunity.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: The motion named Yellow Chase as the site for the Iron Qanat, but the great work was built in the Sobral Grasses instead.

Construct Iron Roundtower.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave, Dragomir Dragovich announced a commission to build the Iron Roundtower, a mithril ministry in Delev near Temeschwar. The commission takes up an opportunity to create such a ministry in Varushka. Its non-standard costs were 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns, with three months needed to complete it. Dragomir provided both the mithril and the crowns after the Summer Solstice of 383YE. Once finished, the ministry will create the title Bargainer of the Iron Tower, a Varushkan national position. It will also affect the amount of mithril going to the public bourse auction at Anvil.

n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Roundtower is described as being built in Delev near Temeschwar, a city held by the League.
n.Varushka: Varushka is to gain a mithril ministry and a new national position, the Bargainer of the Iron Tower, funded by the Varushkan Dragomir Dragovich.

t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is named as the landmark near which the Iron Roundtower is to be built in Delev.

Construct Misericorde Market.d: The self-funded commission required 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, with construction taking three months. Contributions came from Tom Bull (2 crowns, after Autumn Equinox 383YE), Beatrix Amalia De Rondell zu Holberg (16 wains of weirwood, after Winter Solstice) and Lula Kleist von Ennerlund (3 thrones 6 crowns, after Winter Solstice). Once complete, the market creates a lifetime Imperial title, the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market, appointed by unanimous decision of the League senators and revocable by the League Assembly and General Assembly. At the Winter Solstice 383YE an opportunity added a ministry allowing mithril and weirwood to be sold to the orcs for large amounts of herbs, and Holberg business owners would gain a way to diversify into herbs.

n.The League: The League gains a new lifetime Imperial title, the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market, appointed by unanimous consent of its senators and revocable by the League Assembly, along with a route for its merchants to trade mithril and weirwood with the orcs for herbs.

t.Holberg: A covered market was commissioned in Holberg, then held by the Sand Fishers, to let Holberg citizens trade with the orcs, offering local business owners a chance to diversify into herbs.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Misericorde is the site of the new covered market, whose Merchant Prince oversees trade with the Sand Fishers, including a later ministry for exchanging mithril and weirwood for herbs.

Construct Oath's Roots.d: In Summer 383YE a motion was put before the Senate to commission the Oath's Roots, a Bourse seat that would have produced weirwood in Liathaven. It was proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Therunin. The motion was withdrawn, so the Oath's Roots was not established by this motion.

n.Jotun: The Jotun, who held Liathaven at the time, would have gained a weirwood Bourse seat in their territory had the withdrawn motion gone ahead.

t.Liathaven: Liathaven was the proposed site of the Oath's Roots weirwood Bourse seat, but the motion was withdrawn and nothing was built.

Construct Smith of Ashes.d: In Summer 383YE Palerictus Krunk used the Imperial Orc Wayleave to commission a mana sinecure in Skogei Glens, Skarsind, at standard cost. After the Summer Solstice he provided 10 mithril and 20 wains towards the work. Once complete, the sinecure will create a new Imperial title, the Smith of Ashes. The size of the sinecure had not yet been set; that detail was left to the Bearer of the Imperial Wayleave to decide.

n.Imperial Orcs: An Imperial Orc, Palerictus Krunk, used the nation's Wayleave to commission the sinecure in Orc-held Skarsind and paid for its materials himself.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind is to gain a mana sinecure, creating the Imperial title of Smith of Ashes once it is complete.

r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: The Smith of Ashes sinecure is being built in the Skogei Glens, with its size still to be set by the Bearer of the Imperial Wayleave.

Construct Temple of the Winds.d: Proposed by Miekarova and seconded by Morrow, the motion passed in principle in Summer 382YE as part of an opportunity presented by the sword scholars. It cost 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns and three months. Nikolovich Drakov and Edmundo of Damakan's Forge first supplied the materials, but the Druj invasion of Morrow destroyed the site and they received partial refunds. After Peregro was retaken, Edmundo of Damakan's Forge provided the full cost again after the Spring Equinox 383YE and work restarted from scratch. The temple created the title Envoy to the Disciples of the Tempest Jade Maiden. At the Summer Solstice 383YE the Senate passed an amendment making the Labyrinth Sword part of the Master of the Temple of the Winds' regalia, as the sword scholars demanded.

n.Druj: The Druj invasion of Morrow destroyed the first construction site and wiped out all progress, though they were later driven out of Peregro.
n.Urizen: Urizen gained a temple housing the sword scholars in Morrow and a new title, Envoy to the Disciples of the Tempest Jade Maiden, after the Druj destroyed the first attempt to build it.

t.Morrow: Morrow is the site of the Temple of the Winds, a permanent home for the sword scholars. Its construction was destroyed during the Druj invasion and restarted once the territory was partly retaken.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Peregro was recaptured from the Druj in time for construction to begin again without a new motion or commission, though the work had to start from scratch.

Construct Vigilant Shield.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by the senator for Necropolis, the motion sought to create the Vigilant Shield and the title of Captain of the Throne Guard, charged with organising and leading the Throne Guard at Anvil to protect the Throne. The title is appointed annually by the Throne and recallable by the Assembly of Nine and the General Assembly, and is self-funded. Because a sinecure cannot provide liao without an opportunity, the viable constitutional reading was a sinecure providing both votes and liao. Severin Teyhard von Holberg provided 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns after the Summer Solstice.

n.Highguard: Highguard's senators for Reikos and Necropolis proposed and seconded the motion, and the new sinecure is to be built on Highborn soil in Casinea.

t.Casinea: Casinea is to host the Vigilant Shield, a new sinecure providing votes and liao to the Captain of the Throne Guard.

Construct Zoria's Maze.d: Proposed by the Senator for Weirwater and seconded by Ossium, the commission arose from recent interest in Zoria. It was self-funded by the Vor-Azi at a non-standard cost of 18 wains of white granite and 36 crowns, taking three months to complete. Illya Nikovitch Volkov provided the crowns and Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov the granite after the Summer Solstice. The motion states the work will give 18 additional Synod votes. On completion it creates the title Guardian of the Maze of Zoria. The constitutional court suggested either the Varushkan National Assembly or the Assembly of Wisdom as electors, annually or with tenure, and the Weirwater senator favoured annual appointment by the Varushkan National Assembly.

n.Varushka: Varushkans led the project, with Varushkan individuals supplying the crowns and granite, and the Weirwater senator proposed that the Varushkan National Assembly appoint the new Guardian of the Maze of Zoria each year.

t.Miekarova: The maze in the vale of Griejezdo in Miekarova was to be enhanced into a great shrine to Zoria, bringing her recognised resting place new prominence and a new Imperial title.

Construct spy network in the Sarangrave.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Karsk, the motion commissioned a spy network in the Sarangrave and passed at the Summer Solstice 383YE at 40 thrones. The listed costs were 10 weirwood and 20 crowns, with upkeep of 2 crowns per season, though the motion's own text named different sums and Cyrus of Felix's Watch as its funder. After the solstice, Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar provided the 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns. Once complete, the network will allow Imperial military units to support it.

n.Druj: The Empire moved to set up a spy network inside Druj-held land, aimed at gathering intelligence on the orcs of the Mallum.

t.Sarangrave: The Sarangrave was the chosen site for the spy network, and once built it would let Imperial military units support it within the territory despite Druj control.

Declare Ossium orcs as foreigners.d: In Summer 383YE the senator for Ossium proposed, and the senator for Volodmartz seconded, a motion to declare the orc tribes formerly subjugated by the Druj in Ossium to be foreigners in Imperial lands. The motion covered only those orcs of Ossium who are not Druj. It passed, and the orcs of Ossium are now legally foreigners rather than barbarians. The page notes that the decision has implications for the Varushkan settlers in Ossium, though it does not set them out.

n.Druj: The orcs the Druj once held in subjugation in Ossium are now distinguished from them in Imperial law, with the Druj themselves explicitly excluded from foreigner status.
n.Varushka: Varushkan senators for Ossium and Volodmartz proposed and seconded the motion, and its passing has implications for the Varushkan settlers in Ossium.

t.Ossium: The non-Druj orcs living in Varushkan-held Ossium are now recognised as foreigners, which bears on how they and the Varushkan settlers there will live alongside one another.

Drive back.d: Defending Brocéliande required up to 30,000 strength. Military units could Slow the Vallorn for herb payment, and armies could commit up to 15,000 strength each in Boar's Dell and Elerael. Aid came from Dawnish knights, Highborn congregations, the Great Forest Orcs and the eternal Tharim. Zakalwe offered a boon, and Arhallogen and Tharim offered further help at a price. Yaw'nagrah proposed turning the vallorn against the Mallum if Brocéliande were abandoned. Full success could open a chance to clear Dark Ranging. A weirwood forest in the Westwood could be developed for 75 Thrones, with road improvements. A Senate motion to commission the Bourse seat was raised and later withdrawn.

n.Dawn: Ranae de Rondell rallied Dawnish knights-errant and questing knights to fight in Brocéliande, and Dawnish military units were offered bonus rewards for taking part.
n.Druj: The Druj presence made the route from Drycastle impractical. Yaw'nagrah offered to drive the vallorn of Béantal Dol in their lands if the Empire abandoned Brocéliande, and clearing Dark Ranging could also ease any Druj invasion of the territory.
n.Highguard: Answering the call of the Hazelelponi of the Shattered Tower, Highborn congregations sent at least 500 strength to Brocéliande. Tharim offered further aid if allowed to feed on Highguard's herb gardens and forests.
n.Imperial Orcs: A warband of Imperial Orcs discovered the weirwood forest in the Westwood during the campaign to free the region from the vallorn.
n.Jotun: The Jotun still held most of Liathaven, leaving the new weirwood forest precarious. Some urged building a fortification there to guard against their return.
n.Navarr: The Navarr faced the vallorn's strongest surge yet in Brocéliande and paid helpers in herbs. Their herb gardens suffered Tharim's black frost, and many felt Liathaven and its new weirwood should be theirs.
n.The Marches: Weirwood from Liathaven could reach the Mournwold if the Jotun-held regions were freed, which would boost the prosperity of the new market town of Sarcombe.
n.Urizen: The Urizen army, the Citadel Guard, was defending Elerael and could act as a conduit for territory rituals. Its magicians warned against Rivers Run Red and Rivers of Life and noted the value of Wither the Seed.
n.Wintermark: Tharim offered extra aid against the vallorn if the Conclave let him feed on the herb gardens and forests of Wintermark, among other nations, for six months.

t.Astolat: The nobles and yeofolk of Astolat cheered the knights fighting the vallorn, and Yaw'nagrah's emissary appeared near the Castle of Thorns to deliver her bargain.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the only usable roads from West Ranging run north into the deep parts of Bregasland.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn's growing surge threatened to overrun Elerael, Boar's Dell and the Broch. Holding it back completely could open a chance to clear Dark Ranging.
t.Hercynia: A black frost struck Hercynia's herb gardens and drained its forests as Tharim fed in return for his aid against the vallorn.
t.Liathaven: With the vallorn driven from the Westwood, a weirwood forest was found that could become a new Bourse seat. The territory remained largely Jotun-held and troubled by vallornspawn and the Heirs of Terunael.
t.Miaren: Miaren's herb gardens and forests withered under Tharim's black frost, the price of his help in Brocéliande.
t.Mournwold: Weirwood could be carried along the Jotun roads into the Mournwold if Liathaven were liberated, likely bringing caravans and prosperity through Sarcombe.
t.Reikos: Reikos was effectively the only safe route by which Imperial armies could reach Elerael in Brocéliande.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm offered the only safe route for armies into Boar's Dell, and its people cheered the knights fighting the vallorn.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Drycastle is noted as a theoretical route into Boar's Dell, made impractical by the Druj presence.
t.Therunin: Therunin's herb gardens suffered Tharim's black frost. Its senator Cybi Farkas called the Great Forest Orcs to send warriors to Brocéliande.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named; the page only notes that the roads from West Ranging lead north into the darkest parts of Bregasland.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Boar's Dell faced being overrun by the vallorn. Armies reaching it from Semmerholm could contribute up to 15,000 strength to its defence, at around 1,500 casualties.
r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: If the vallorn were held back completely, the Empire would have at least six months to try to clear Dark Ranging, extendable by a curse such as Wither the Seed.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Elerael, defended by the Citadel Guard, faced the vallorn's surge. Armies arriving via Reikos could commit up to 15,000 strength there.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: Freeing Liath's Ring from the Jotun would open their fine roads for carrying weirwood to the Mournwold, raising the forest's output.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: Liberating Liaven's Glen from the Jotun would let weirwood travel the Jotun roads to Green March or Southmoor.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The Empire held West Ranging only by the slenderest margin. A road linking it to the Westwood forest could raise weirwood output, but losing it would isolate the forest.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Now cleared of the vallorn, the Westwood held a pristine weirwood grove. Establishing it as a Bourse resource would cost 75 Thrones and could yield 12 to 24 wains a season.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Green March was a possible destination for weirwood caravans if the Jotun-held regions of Liathaven were liberated.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: The Jotun-built paved road through West Ranging runs to Southmoor, which could receive weirwood caravans if Liathaven were freed.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named; Therunin as a whole is noted for Tharim's black frost and the Great Forest Orcs' aid.

Four strong winds.d: The opportunities were a mithril exchange, the Parador of Dust, in Kahraman; the Zeinodin Caravanserai, to be built in Segura once Anduz is freed; a renewed Iron Qanat for the Sobral Grasses; Zemress Islander payments to Imperial units fighting in Segura; a salvage Haven of Peredio; and relocating the Broken Shore Bounty offices out of Grendel-held Cazar. The Prosperity Assembly's condemnation of Lasambrian plunder angered corsairs, and two competing mandates followed. The Senate commissioned the Iron Qanat and sanctioned the House of Guerra. The Assembly sent Mazo i Zabala i Erigo to rally Segura's defence and Efenia i Maristela i Riqueza to champion privateering over trade. The Bounty stayed in Cazar, and the caravanserai remained available in Summer 384YE.

n.Grendel: The Grendel invasion of Feroz left the Broken Shore Bounty offices in Cazar in their hands, where they remained. Their weirwood-carrying ships were named as prey for corsairs, and the Assembly's mandate pushed Freeborn captains towards privateering against them.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Cinderpath Exchange in Casinea, whose construction began with rumblings among the Highborn, served as the model for the Parador of Dust, and the i Orieni had ties with fishing families in southern Highguard.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun held Anduzjasse and parts of Anozeseri, and the Prosperity Assembly condemned them for taking rather than earning. The Zemress Islanders offered to pay Imperial units to fight them, and the Assembly sent a priest to rally Segura's defence.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a slate of opportunities, from a mithril exchange to a fortified caravanserai, and saw the Iron Qanat and House of Guerra sanctioned. Their corsairs were angered by the Prosperity statement until the Assembly's mandate endorsed privateering over trade.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the i Orieni family who ran the Broken Shore Bounty had ties with fishing and mercantile families in the southern territories of Urizen.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Roundtower in Varushka was cited as a similar commission that reduces the mithril offered at the public auction.

t.Bay of Catazar: An Assembly statement urged the Freeborn to search the bay for salvageable weirwood, and the corsair Isidore proposed a haven on Peredio to gather salvage and captured Grendel weirwood. The bay's fishing nets are also the source of the Broken Shore Bounty's ilium.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the successful Cinderpath Exchange in Casinea inspired the proposed Parador of Dust in Kahraman.
t.Feroz: Grendel-occupied Cazar still housed the Broken Shore Bounty offices, which remained there in the Grendel's notional hands. The page warned that moving them would have damaged the morale of the corsair families and people of Feroz.
t.Kahraman: The i Liscano family proposed the Parador of Dust as a mithril exchange for the territory's mines, costing 16 white granite, 32 crowns and a Senate motion or wayleave. Kahraman hakima Chiara i Erigo led the case for celebrating privateering.
t.Madruga: The only Brass Coast territory not threatened by barbarians, Madruga was encouraged to build a hostelry, and there was talk there of urgently re-establishing the Broken Shore Bounty. The proposed Haven of Peredio would lie on an island where Madruga merges into the open sea.
t.Segura: The architect Angelina i Duarte i Riqueza proposed the Zeinodin Caravanserai, and the Senate commissioned the Iron Qanat. The Assembly also sent a priest to encourage soldiers to fight for the territory, backed by Islander payments to units supporting armies there.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Broken Shore Bounty offices remained in Grendel-held Cazar. Moving them would have signalled that the Senate doubted the Cazar Straits corsairs could protect them, a blow to the i Orieni family.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The i Liscano parador in the western Jade Range, beside a major road towards Segura and Madruga, was proposed as the site of the Parador of Dust mithril exchange.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: The mithril-bearing hills of Serra Briante, home to the Great Mine of Briante, are one of the sources the Parador of Dust was meant to draw on.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Damatian Cliffs and the mines of Serra Damata, whose occasional mithril finds reach the town of Damata, would supply the proposed Parador of Dust.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Mentioned in passing: the corsair Isidore i Boyaga i Erigo put into harbour at Free Landing just long enough to propose the Haven of Peredio.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Conquered by the Jotun, Anduzjasse was where the Zeinodin Caravanserai would be built at the heart of the region once Anduz is freed. The caravanserai would cost 75 wains of white granite, 150 crowns and a Senate motion, and would pay the units that defend it.
r.Segura/Anozeseri: Parts of Anozeseri were held by the Jotun, so the Zemress Islanders' farms elsewhere in Segura were not under occupation, despite the wording of the Assembly's judgement.
r.Segura/Burnish: Mentioned in passing: fortifying Burnish was listed among Angelina i Duarte i Riqueza's plans for Segura.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The Zemress Islanders revived the Iron Qanat to irrigate the sandy soils of the Grasses, allowing the Freeborn to support one more army or navy. The Senate commissioned it this season.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: Mentioned in passing: Yellow Chase is one of the regions where the Zemress Islanders were given lands, which were not occupied by the Jotun.

Heart of gold.d: Naomi found that the thralls' pacifism meant inducting them would not give the Marches a fifth army, though clearing Alderly's forest via a Senate-commissioned sawmill could. Inducting them would bring a small rise in taxation and reduce a defensive risk. Their children who choose to become warriors might instead be encouraged to join the Imperial Orcs. However, the thralls believe orcs reincarnate, which is heresy, and Naomi advised against bonding them until this was resolved. The Whittle folk, led by Bill Tavistock, would turn violently on the orcs, and she suggested dealing with them before or after. At Summer Solstice the Marcher Assembly condemned Whittle's Hate and endorsed closer contact, while the Imperial Orcs sent Bloodcrow Udoo to welcome thrall children.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly was offered a mandate to draw warrior-minded thrall children into their nation, and they sent Bloodcrow Udoo to reassure the thralls that their children were welcome in the north, though such children would hear the Jotun ancestors.
n.Jotun: The Mournwold orcs remain loyal to the Jotun jarls and some of their children slip west to join Jotun warbands, which Naomi judged a defensive risk that bonding them to the Marches would curtail.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr were suggested as particularly helpful in guiding Mournwold orc youths towards the Imperial Orcs, given their experience of the Great Dance.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is cited as a neighbouring land with which Mournwold Marchers have less in common than with the thralls.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is cited as a neighbouring land with which Mournwold Marchers have less in common than with the thralls.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly gained an open, irreversible mandate to have Jack bond the Mournwold orcs to the nation, and at Summer Solstice it demanded the Whittle folk abandon Hate and endorsed greater contact with the thralls.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the mora of Varushka are cited in an out-of-character note as an example of a non-playable people.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: an out-of-character note cites the hylje of Wintermark and states the thralls could never join Wintermark, being so unlike it culturally.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Orrick, Senator of Bregasland, co-wrote missives urging the Mournwold orc leaders to cooperate and attend Anvil.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: named as a land across the border with which Mournwold folk share less than with the thralls.
t.Mournwold: The territory's thralls might become Marchers, raising taxes and easing the risk of welcoming a Jotun return, but their heretical belief in reincarnation and Whittle's violent hatred, voiced by Bill Tavistock, threaten bloodshed and possible executions; the thralls declined to attend Summer Solstice but might come at Autumn.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: named as a land across the border with which Mournwold folk share less than with the thralls.

r.Mournwold/Alderly: With the Feni driven off, Alderly's fertile forest could be cleared over a year to let the Marches raise a fifth army, requiring a Senate-built sawmill at Alderly Edge costing 20 wains of weirwood, 5 of mithril and 50 crowns, which would create the Woodcutter of Alderly Edge title.

Living with war.d: Imperial fleets had battered Grendel pirates in the Bay of Catazar, leaving wrecked crews ashore at the Golden Keys in Free Landing and at Letivius Station in Apulus. In the East Floes of Sermersuaq, four Jotun stockades showed signs of unrest, possibly linked to thrall resistance. In Brocéliande, Urizen sentinels carrying Vital Honey were trapped at Exile Trod, and a monstrous dire canthon menaced Deep Weaver Wood. Ser Ancél Watcher's questing knights located Druj miasma pillars at Lomaa Spoils and Tanglethorn Glade in Ossium. Druj tortured souls, likely former Dawnish citizens, attacked Varushkan settlers at Korlack Marsh. Druj raiders had followed the victorious armies into Misericorde and camped at Semmerpine Shore.

n.Dawn: Dawnish knights led by Ser Ancél Watcher found two Druj miasma pillars in Ossium, Dawn's warriors were invited to slay a dire canthon in Boar's Dell, and its priests were called to exorcise tortured souls who were likely Dawnish captives from Dawnguard.
n.Druj: Druj miasma pillars still blanket Ossium, Druj bands with tortured souls raided Varushkan settlers at Korlack Marsh, and a Druj scouting party has camped secretly at Semmerpine Shore in Holberg.
n.Grendel: Grendel pirates were badly mauled across the Bay of Catazar, and two stranded crews, one raiding Free Landing and one holding Letivius Station in Spiral, were left vulnerable to Imperial strikes.
n.Highguard: Highguard was among the nations called on to join the Saturday strikes against the vallorn at Exile Trod and Deep Weaver Wood in Brocéliande.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the peaks of Skarsind are named as one end of the long Jotun border that the barbarians cannot fully secure.
n.Jotun: Although they hold most of Sermersuaq, the Jotun cannot secure its long border, and their four stockades in the East Floes are troubled by supply disruptions, quarrels and possible thrall resistance.
n.Navarr: Navarr efforts to stop the vallorn spreading into Elerael and Boar's Dell held for a third season, with chances to thin the husk hordes and rescue trapped sentinels.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn corsairs helped sink Grendel ships, and a desperate band of shipwrecked marines raided settlements near the Golden Keys before being driven off, offering a chance to destroy them.
n.The League: A Druj raiding band has slipped into Holberg's Misericorde forests and may learn about the Sand Fishers' new home or the city's strengthened defences unless it is dealt with.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named; the page concerns Ossium only through Dawnish and Varushkan efforts against the Druj.
n.Urizen: Urizen was called to attack the Grendel pirates holding Letivius Station in Spiral, while its Citadel Guard gathered mana in Brocéliande and some of its sentinels were trapped with Vital Honey at Exile Trod.
