n.Varushka: Varushkan settlers in Ossium face Druj skirmishers and the tortured souls that destroyed hamlets around Korlack Marsh, prompting initial false rumours of Dawnish treachery.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk near the border secretly supply Suaq thralls under Jotun rule, and Icewalkers reported four troubled Jotun stockades where Suaq cunning could aid strikes and uncover thrall resistance.

t.Bay of Catazar: Imperial fleet owners and privateers sank, scuttled and captured many Grendel ships, leaving wreckage and bodies of Grendel sailors washing ashore across the Bay.
t.Brocéliande: Imperial forces held back the vallorn for a third season, and two conjunctions offered chances to rescue trapped sentinels and kill a monstrous dire canthon while thinning the husk hordes.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: its hills form part of the Sermersuaq border that the Jotun cannot fully secure.
t.Holberg: A Druj band that followed the armies out of Ossium is camped at Semmerpine Shore and could scout the Sand Fishers' new lands and Holberg's defences if not defeated.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: its marshes mark one end of the porous Jotun-held border of Sermersuaq.
t.Madruga: Shipwrecked Grendel marines landed near the Golden Keys and twice raided local settlements before retreating, leaving a chance to destroy them before they escape by sea.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the stranded pirates in Spiral may try to cross the border into Mareave.
t.Ossium: Druj miasma pillars still shroud most of the territory, two were located by Dawnish knights, and Druj raiders with tortured souls continue to threaten Varushkan settlers.
t.Sermersuaq: Under Jotun rule, Suaq thralls endure hard but bearable lives, and four Jotun stockades in the East Floes show signs of unrest that Imperial forces were invited to exploit.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: its peaks are named as part of the long border with Jotun-held Sermersuaq.
t.Spiral: A wrecked Grendel crew seized Letivius Station near Apulian, and any strike against them must contend with the Black Plateau miasma.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: A dire canthon, a giant Spring-infused beetle able to shatter lances, was reported in Deep Weaver Wood, and Dawn's warriors were offered a chance to slay it.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Sentinels who had found a large store of Vital Honey were trapped by husks at Exile Trod, and destroying the horde there would help hold back the vallorn next season.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Druj raiders crept through Misericorde's dark forests and made a fireless, picketed camp at Semmerpine Shore on the Semmerlak.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Grendel marines wrecked near the Golden Keys raided local settlements for money and supplies, but they were repelled and now seek a way to escape.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Scattered parts of the Bittershore are free of miasma because its pillar at Scarred Bay was destroyed last year, and the victorious armies crossed the Barrens River from there.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Mentioned in passing: its miasma pillar has yet to be discovered.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Druj Chikad warriors and tortured souls destroyed several hamlets and farms around Korlack Marsh, and priests skilled in exorcism were sought to banish them.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Mentioned in passing: its miasma pillar remains undiscovered.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: Ser Ancél's knights located a Druj miasma pillar at Lomaa Spoils near the mithril mine, which could be broken by Chimes of Annulment or priestly consecration.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Mentioned in passing: its miasma pillar is already known to stand at Fang Tree.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Rumours of thrall rebellion are spreading, and four Jotun stockades here, Thenga's Camp, the Hall of Crows, Arroweye's Fast and Bearer's Rest, were identified as targets for Imperial strikes and investigation.
r.Spiral/Apulus: A stranded Grendel crew seized Letivius Station, guarding the approaches to ruined Apulian, and are disorganised and vulnerable while still under the Black Plateau miasma.

Long walk home.d: Nearly forty captains, aided by the Winter Sun, the Great Forest orcs and briars, and heralds of the Golden Hare, brought all the recovered Dubhtraig slaves to Skarsind, boosting Imperial Orc production for two seasons. The Holt of the Oak neared completion, and the briars sought Senate permission to refine liao from material salvaged at the lost Liao Garden. The Thule released about a hundred slaves, freed Snowstorm Henk and alleged that Imperials murdered a Krevsaty mine owner. They also built fortifications at supernatural speed. Jarl Geir's warband collected the 200-throne weregild. In the end the Senate ratified a Thule treaty ceding Sungold Pass and made the Fleet Master responsible for Grendel diplomacy.

n.Dawn: Eadric Fjellrevening, knight-errant of House de Rondell, led the expedition that uncovered the lost Liao Garden. About a hundred and fifty freed orcs headed to Astolat, where the Winter Sun were billeted, seeking land in return for military service.
n.Grendel: Salt Lord Moorvain of Vorlach demanded that the Empire recognise a worthy ambassador, namely the Imperial Fleet Master, before any talk of Feroz's surrender. The Grendel refused to deal with the Imperial Consul, and the Senate later granted the Fleet Master responsibility for Grendel diplomacy.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc captains and the Winter Sun led the effort to bring the freed Dubhtraig orcs home to Skarsind, and their assembly's mandate rewarded the captains. Every Imperial Orc owning a business, farm, forest or herb garden gains a rank of production until the Winter Solstice.
n.Jotun: A Jotun delegation had agreed a weregild of 200 thrones for those killed at the Meeting Place. Jarl Geir the Iron Bull then led a kirkja warband to Anvil to compete for a Wintermark shield, and the warband returned home with the two hundred Throne pieces.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were the only nation not to aid the rescue of the freed orcs, being occupied with the vallorn and joined by Great Forest warriors in Brocéliande. The briars' liao proposal would involve Navarr traders and possibly a Navarr-appointed overseer of a new sinecure.
n.The Brass Coast: The Grendel's invasion of Feroz continued and they spoke of discussing its surrender. They demanded the Fleet Master, Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra, as their ambassador, and the Senate granted that title responsibility for Grendel diplomacy.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel message arrived in Sarvos, lost orcs were found in the forests of Temeschwar, and the Sand Fishers' settlement in Holberg is referenced.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: lost orcs were found in Bregasland, and developments with the Mournwold thralls are referenced elsewhere.
n.Thule: The Thule released around a hundred Imperial slaves and Snowstorm Henk, but they still chafe under sanctions and allege that Imperials murdered a Krevsaty mine owner. They are rapidly fortifying Ossium, Karsk and Skarsind, and the Senate later ratified a treaty ceding Sungold Pass to them.
n.Varushka: Yevgeni Katzev of Varushka, Ambassador to Otkodov, was invited to the Caucus Forum and to investigate the Krevsaty murder. Freed slaves arrived at Wendell's Hope, and the Thule continued to build fortifications in Ossium and Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's mediators had agreed the Jotun weregild, and Jarl Geir's warband came to compete in the Winterfolk shield contest. Freed Thule slaves travelled west seeking Erska Crowspeaker and were met by the Wintermark egregore.

t.Astolat: Around a hundred and fifty freed orcs set out for Astolat, where the Winter Sun were billeted, drawn by the offer of land in return for military service.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Empire had mounted a convincing challenge to Grendel supremacy in the bay.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: heralds of the Golden Hare found lost orcs here.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: most Great Forest orc warriors had gone to aid the Navarr here.
t.Feroz: The Grendel invasion continued, and the Grendel demanded a worthy ambassador with whom to discuss the territory's surrender.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the territory is linked to Wintermark's affairs this season, including the Jotun contest and freed slaves heading west to the 'Mark.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: heralds of the Golden Hare found lost orcs here.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers are noted as settling into new homes here.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: heralds of the Golden Hare found lost orcs here.
t.Karsk: The Thule alleged that Imperial raiders killed mine owner Thuli in Krevsaty and stole slaves. Their fortification there is expected to be completed by the Autumn Equinox.
t.Miekarova: About a hundred released Imperial slaves were left at Wendell's Hope, where the civil service helped them, though many chose to head on to Wintermark.
t.Mountains of the Moon: The people of Tsark located and dismantled the entire Imperial spy network, leaving the Empire with no knowledge of events there.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: developments with the Mournwold thralls are referenced in further reading.
t.Ossium: A major Thule force remained as the only significant army in the territory, and their Bonewood fortification was already half built.
t.Otkodov: The orcs of Otkodov chafed under trade sanctions while still claiming Sungold Pass, which the Senate later ceded to them by treaty.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel message from Salt Lord Moorvain was received here.
t.Sermersuaq: The new Thule castle at Crow's Keep has watchtowers overlooking the passes into the Silver Peaks, and the dispute over Sungold Pass ended with the pass being ceded to Otkodov.
t.Shayeel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel holding it issued their diplomatic demand, though the territory itself is not named.
t.Skarsind: The freed Dubhtraig orcs were brought to Gildenheim and found new lives across the territory. The Thule completed their castle at Crow's Keep, with garrisons overlooking Urdur and the Silver Peaks.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: lost orcs were found in its forests by heralds of the Golden Hare.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest orcs continued making the territory their home as the Holt of the Oak neared completion. The briars sought permission to refine liao there, and about twenty freed orcs chose to settle among them.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Thuli's mine was allegedly raided by Imperials who killed the owner and stole slaves, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction offered four investigators a chance to examine the evidence. Meanwhile, the Thule fort in the hills neared completion.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Released Imperial slaves were deposited at Wendell's Hope with a note saying they had been purchased by Erska Crowspeaker.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Thule began a fortification here that scouts reported half complete after only three months.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Mentioned in passing: watchtowers of the new Thule castle at Crow's Keep overlook the passes into Urdur.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the wider Thule frontier dispute, including Sungold Pass, forms the backdrop.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Thule watchtowers and garrisons around Crow's Keep now overlook the passes into the Silver Peaks from the east.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Work on the Holt of the Oak continued and was due shortly before the Winter Solstice. The briars there proposed a liao workshop and named Ursol Gwin as their point of contact.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Eadric Fjellrevening's expedition uncovered the lost Liao Garden near Sweetglades, cleared vallornspawn, and enabled the recovery of preserved vinum sap and refining equipment.

Old ways.d: With the Basilica of Seven Doors refurbished and the Highborn Speaker restored, several opportunities were proposed. The bishops of Sarvos suggested refurbishing Capodomus Cathedral to create a title guiding the League assembly, with its name still disputed between Archbishop, Speaker or Bishop. Wintermark priests proposed rebuilding the Hall of Rund in Kallavesa, possibly as the seat of the Speaker of the Crows. Abbot Matilda of Becktunn urged a seminary honouring the Exemplar Margaret of Meade to help Marchers win Imperial titles. Varushkan wise ones suggested expanding the Tender of the Hearth's duties by Senate motion. Other assemblies, such as Dawn and Navarr, might pursue similar titles through statements of principle. The opportunities remain open until at least the Autumn Equinox.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the troubadours of Dawn were given as an example of an assembly that might seek a First Troubadour seated at Laroc Cathedral.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel were recalled as having stolen Capodomus Cathedral's artworks and damaged it during the sack of Sarvos.
n.Highguard: The restored Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, custodian of the Basilica of Seven Doors, became the model that other national assemblies now considered copying.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr assembly was suggested as one that might announce the intent to create a Priests' Brand.
n.The League: League bishops proposed refurbishing Capodomus Cathedral to create a title guiding the League assembly. That title would carry 20 Synod votes, 10 liao and 7 crowns each season, though priests continued to squabble over what it should be called.
n.The Marches: Abbot Matilda proposed building the Seminary of Margaret's Oak, whose prior would encourage and help Marchers win Imperial titles and revive the forgotten legacy of the Exemplar Margaret of Meade.
n.Varushka: Varushkan wise ones suggested a Senate motion to make the Tender of the Hearth an annual national assembly appointment. The expanded role would guide the assembly and would gain an extra dose of liao and two extra votes.
n.Wintermark: Amid renewed interest in priests acting in the Synod, Wintermark could rebuild the Hall of Rund to create a title guiding its assembly with 18 liao. That title might become an official Speaker of the Crows advising the Thane's Council.

t.Bastion: The refurbished Basilica of Seven Doors in Bastion, completed shortly before the Summer Solstice, restored the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly to prominence.
t.Kallavesa: The ancient Hall of Rund in Rundhal, birthplace of the stormcrow tradition, could be rebuilt upwards with weirwood and white granite to house all Wintermark's priests once more.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: wise ones from Karov were among those suggesting the Tender of the Hearth's responsibilities be expanded.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: wise ones from Karsk were among those suggesting the Tender of the Hearth's responsibilities be expanded.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Margaret of Meade was recalled as having served as Senator for Mitwold on and off for two decades.
t.Sarvos: Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos, damaged and looted in the Grendel sack, could be refurbished as the seat of the League assembly's new leader and filled with new artwork from across the League.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Margaret of Meade argued that cities such as Tassato were luring skilled yeomen away from the Marches.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: wise ones from Volodmartz were among those suggesting the Tender of the Hearth's responsibilities be expanded.

Raise Thornbound Army of Navarr.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Bastion, the motion called for a self-funded commission at non-standard cost: 200 wains of mithril, 50 wains of weirwood and 500 crowns, taking a year to complete. Contributions began after the Summer Solstice 383YE and continued through the Winter Solstice. Major donors included Corey Wayfarer, Gwendolyn Splinterspear and Rhisiart Heartsbane, with a smaller gift from Lleu Winter's Reach. The recorded donations add up to the full 200 wains of mithril and 50 wains of weirwood, alongside money. When the commission is complete, a third Navarr army with the Thornbound quality will be raised.

n.Navarr: Navarr stands to gain a third army with the Thornbound quality, largely paid for by mithril, weirwood and coin given by Navarri donors, through an opportunity presented by the nation's vates.

t.Miaren: Miaren is named as the place where the new Thornbound army is to be mustered once the year-long commission is complete.

Ratify Sungold Treaty.d: Proposed by Karsk and seconded by Temeschwar, the motion ratified a treaty under which the Empire ceded the Sungold Pass to the Thule orcs and the Senate paid 300 Thrones. In return, the Thule would return 2900 Imperial slaves and all Navarri citizens, and defend Ossium for the next season. The Thule queried two points of wording: they understood the treaty to recognise that Sungold Pass lay in Otkodov, not that it was Imperial land ceded to them, and they understood the Navarr artisans were to be released in return for that recognition rather than for payment.

n.Navarr: All Navarri citizens held by the Thule were to be freed under the treaty, though the Thule understood the Navarr artisans' release to be in exchange for recognising Sungold Pass as part of Otkodov.
n.Thule: The Thule orcs gained the Sungold Pass and 300 Thrones, agreeing in return to free 2900 Imperial slaves and all Navarri citizens and to defend Ossium for a season, while disputing how the treaty described the Pass.
n.Varushka: Varushkan-held Ossium was to be defended by the Thule for the next season, and the Varushkan senator for Karsk proposed the motion.

t.Ossium: The Thule committed to defend Ossium, then held by Varushka, for the season following the treaty.
t.Otkodov: The Sungold Pass passed to the Thule, who held Otkodov and understood the treaty as recognising the Pass as part of that territory rather than as Imperial land ceded to them.

Sun green.d: Stars vanished over the Barrens, Spiral, Zenith, Holberg, Ossium and Semmerholm, impeding divination and making naga there more secretive. The Penumbral Veil covered Thule's lands, while the shrouds over Feroz, Temeschwar and Morrow faded. Summer Dawning Relentless raised ice castles in Ankra, Ateri and Estmure, and the Sussavari Frost Coven raised one in the North Fens and performed Wondrous Forests of the Night. Ashen Flame created the Three Watchers. Cathan Canae, Callidus, Agramant, Sung and the Black Tablet made offers to the Conclave. In the resolution, the Conclave passed declarations on necromancy and on Wintermark's strength, so ice-giant warbands now guard the beacons. Dawn's apology to Adamant lacked a greater majority.

n.Dawn: Summer Dawning Relentless raised three ice castles and had earlier sent Knights of Glory against the Barrens. Alexander of House Tallstag was offered a Summer draught, and Dawn's failure to thank Adamant for the Gates of Adamant left his koboldi hinting at disappointment, with Mordred's apology falling short of a greater majority.
n.Druj: Every territory under the starless skies is occupied by or of obvious interest to the Druj, raising fears of what else they can do, and the new ice castles appear intended to defend against them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Spiral, which it shares with Urizen, lies under the starless sky and now hosts two of Dawn's ice castles.
n.Highguard: The Three Watchers now memorialise Highborn sacrifice and are expected to draw Highborn pilgrims. A Necropolis chapter pressed for oversight of necromancy, and the chapter of Zephaniah's Lament was struck by a withering curse.
n.Jotun: Cathan Canae's ice giants were sent to help guard the beacons of Kallavesa and Hahnmark specifically to keep the Jotun out of Wintermark.
n.The Brass Coast: The shroud that had hung over Feroz faded away. Callidus sought out the Autumn Archmage, Edmundo of Damakan's Forge, about his Tassato request.
n.The League: Holberg remained starless and Temeschwar's shroud lifted. Callidus asked for the Freedom of the City in Cascatas, Tassato, a request that would raise the territory's taxes if granted.
n.The Marches: A Wintermark coven raised a protective citadel in Bregasland's North Fens. Cathan Canae entrusted Will Talbot with a ritual that grants dangerous strength to Marcher halberdiers for a year.
n.Thule: The Thule kept the Penumbral Veil over Urdur, Nithoggir, Sküld and Verthandi, impeding Imperial divination of their lands.
n.Urizen: The Urizen coven Ashen Flame created the Three Watchers in Morrow at Furia Severia's direction, and the shroud over Morrow faded.
n.Varushka: The stars went out over Varushka's Ossium. Cathan Canae praised the Varushkans and Dawnish who took Ossium from the Druj.
n.Wintermark: The Sussavari Frost Coven performed Wondrous Forests of the Night and raised a citadel in the North Fens. After the Conclave recognised Wintermark's strength, Cathan Canae sent ice-giant warbands to guard the beacons of Kallavesa and Hahnmark.

t.Bregasland: A magical citadel of mist and fog was raised in the North Fens, protecting the Dour Fens until the Summer Solstice.
t.Feroz: The shroud that previously hung over Feroz faded away.
t.Hahnmark: A warband of Cathan Canae's ice giants was sent to help guard Hahnmark's beacons against the Jotun.
t.Holberg: The night skies over Holberg stayed starless, divination there was impeded, and naga who spent time there felt a strong urge to secrecy.
t.Kallavesa: A warband of Cathan Canae's ice giants was sent to help guard Kallavesa's beacons against the Jotun.
t.Morrow: Three statues nearly two hundred feet tall now guard the pass from Morrow to Zenith, with a liao-consecrated shrine of Loyalty, and Morrow's shroud has lifted.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Black Tablet, which proposed support for the Imperial Necromancer, is a Necropolis chapter.
t.Ossium: After the Spring Equinox the stars over Ossium flickered out, impeding divination and affecting naga who stay there.
t.Otkodov: The Penumbral Veil hung over Urdur, Nithoggir and Sküld, shrouding Otkodov from scrying.
t.Semmerholm: The stars went out over Semmerholm and an ice castle was raised in Estmure. The Gates of Adamant there became a point of friction with the eternal who built them.
t.Spiral: Spiral's skies stayed starless, and ice castles were raised in Ankra and Ateri, though the Druj did not attack there.
t.Tassato: Callidus sought the Freedom of the City in Cascatas, and his herald turned up at the Edmundo's Forge tavern looking for the Autumn Archmage.
t.Temeschwar: The shroud that previously hung over Temeschwar faded away.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens remained starless and shrouded, and Dawn's Knights of Glory had been called to aid the attack there in Spring.
t.Verthandi: The Penumbral Veil was reported over Verthandi, impeding divination of the territory.
t.Zenith: Zenith's skies stayed starless, and the Three Watchers now loom over the pass leading into it from Morrow.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Sussavari Frost Coven raised a citadel of mist and fog here, sheltering defenders and travellers until the Summer Solstice.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: Nithoggir lay under the Penumbral Veil, impeding divination.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Sküld lay under the Penumbral Veil, impeding divination.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: The Penumbral Veil still hung over Urdur, according to Imperial merchants.
r.Semmerholm/Estmure: An enchanted citadel of stone and ice was called up in the hills of Estmure by Summer Dawning Relentless.
r.Spiral/Ankra: An ice castle from the Lady of the Frost's domain was raised in the hills of Ankra.
r.Spiral/Ateri: An ice castle from the Lady of the Frost's domain was raised in the hills of Ateri.
r.Tassato/Cascatas: Callidus asked the Conclave for the Freedom of the City here, which would let his heralds come and go and raise Tassato's taxes by one throne each season, cumulatively; it remained only an offer.

Through my sails.d: The Iron Confederacy executed ten Imperial citizens in Robec for alleged espionage. It kept its embargo, replaced its embassy staff in Sarvos and named the secular Baroness Lavasse as its voice, while still angered by the fine imposed on the Highborn behind the border killings. A Freeborn raid in Afarjasse broke a liao smuggling route. In Asavea a mob wrecked the Temple of the Seven Virtues in Nemoria after the Synod defaced Oktístis's works, and the northern rebellion collapsed. The Sarcophan offered land for an Imperial enclave in the Delves. The Faraden gained a blight cure and offered mithril to the Conclave. The Sumaah proposed a symposium on the Way.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish noble Ser Flora Du Soleil was among the ten Imperial citizens executed by the Iron Confederacy, and Dawn remained a possible site for a Kruidenkenner herb warehouse.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Synod statement blamed dealings with the Grendel and Druj for Axos's false expectations of orcs.
n.Grendel: The Grendel were letting Asavean merchants dock at the temple in Feroz, and the goodwill Imperial captains drew from it was likely to shift to the Grendel if Oran stayed in their hands for another season.
n.Highguard: The Iron Confederacy denounced the fine levied on Mordecai of Zephaniah's Lament and the other Highborn who killed its templars as an insult, and the matter ended talks on a criminal extradition treaty. The Highborn Accalon of Felix's Watch served as ambassador to the Sumaah.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Synod specifically called on Imperial Orc traders to show Axos their prosperity, offering an alternative to the example the Axou had seen in the Grendel and Druj.
n.Jotun: The Jotun charged Faraden traders a tithe to cross the Lasambrian Hills, and the page suggested that disaffected Faraden merchants might increasingly trade with the Jotun, who were at peace with them.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Hearc Stormsailor was executed in the Iron Confederacy, and the Kruidenkenner added Seren in Miaren as a possible site for a herb warehouse.
n.The Brass Coast: Four Freeborn were executed by the Suranni and the land border to the Confederacy stayed closed. Freeborn magistrates and militia destroyed a liao smuggling route through Feroz, and rumours persisted of Faraden smugglers slipping through Segura and Kahraman.
n.The League: Three League citizens were executed in Robec and the Suranni embassy in Sarvos saw its staff abruptly replaced. The Sarcophan asked that their own enclave be built in Sarvos or Karsk, and League citizens served as ambassadors to Faraden and the Commonwealth.
n.The Marches: The Senate had approved a Kruidenkenner warehouse at Meade in Mitwold to import Bladeroot from the Sarcophan Delves.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the page said developments involving the orc nations were covered elsewhere, and named Otkodov only as one of the Empire's smaller neighbours.
n.Urizen: Tarquinius Ankarien of Urizen, Ambassador to Axos, was sent by the Synod's enacted mandate to urge Imperial citizens to trade with the Axou.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark ship captain Jayce Audricsson was executed by the Suranni. Wintermark citizens held the ambassadorships to the Sarcophan Delves and to Jarm, and Wintermark remained a possible site for a Kruidenkenner warehouse.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Axos trade mandate could inspire the territories along the Bay of Catazar if 50 doses of liao were committed.
t.Feroz: A liao smuggling route into the Iron Confederacy via Feroz was destroyed. The Imperial-Asavean temple there still stood, but with Oran in Grendel hands its benefits risked being lost, and the ongoing fighting deterred Suranni merchants.
t.Kahraman: Rumours persisted, still unconfirmed, that Faraden smugglers were entering the Empire through southern Kahraman to avoid tariffs.
t.Kalino: Baroness Lavasse advised the Suranni Dukes to secure the northern border of Arbonne, which the Empire calls Kalino, and chastised Duke Harold Guiscard for failing to do so.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga was not named; the page referred only to the closed land border from the southern Brass Coast.
t.Miaren: The Kruidenkenner herbalists added the city of Seren in Miaren as a possible warehouse site because of its central location, an opportunity open until the end of the Summer Solstice.
t.Mitwold: The Senate had approved a Kruidenkenner warehouse at Meade, focused on importing Bladeroot.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis was not named; Highguard's only link on the page is the fine levied on the Highborn involved in the border incident.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov was listed as one of four smaller neighbours close enough to affect Imperial politics, with orc developments covered elsewhere.
t.Sarvos: The Suranni embassy in Sarvos was emptied and restaffed with new ambassadors, who announced that the High Priest would burn messages from Imperial citizens. The Sarcophan also asked for their own enclave to be built in Sarvos or Karsk.
t.Segura: Unconfirmed reports of Faraden smugglers in northern Segura persisted, and the ongoing conflict there was discouraging Suranni merchants from coming north.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Following a raid on a criminal stronghold during the Equinox, Freeborn magistrates and militia stormed a parador in Afarjasse and arrested members of the liao smuggling ring.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: Meade was the site of the Senate-approved Kruidenkenner warehouse importing Bladeroot from the Sarcophan Delves.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach was not named on the page.

Touch the night.d: The magnitude 160 ritual, only the third such Empire-wide enchantment since before Emperor Hugh, boosted every forest's produce. Naga could strengthen their lineage trappings, gained an extra hero point and felt drawn to avarice and indifference to others, and more naga children are expected. Valeria of the Cloistered Eye catalogued altered rituals, including doubled alchemical transmutations and a cheaper Still Waters, Running Deep, while Wondrous Forests itself rose to magnitude 200. Azoth offered alchemical talismans. Lashonar offered nine Jarmish quills for ambassadors. Janon's herald Spark sought to talk faith. The Whisper Gallery offered to lift one enmity in exchange for a stolen ritual text. Sung offered three motes. The Conclave accepted the boons of Lashonar and Sung.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named directly, though heralds of Azoth are said to have visited the Castle of Thorns to offer their alchemical aid.
n.Highguard: Caleb of the Cenotaph, Minister of Historical Research, remained on the Whisper Gallery's list of Arch-Offenders whose deaths they sought, with a reward offered for his heart at the Summer Solstice.
n.Navarr: Two Navarr title-holders, Hywel Summercrow as Cardinal of the Way and Siân of the Eternal Family as Advisor on the Vallorn, stood on the Whisper Gallery's list of Arch-Offenders marked for death, though the Court offered to lift one enmity if its stolen ritual were returned.
n.The League: The League's Jaffo di Tassato suffered a botched transmutation in the opening tale, and Janon's herald Spark specifically sought a conversation with Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato about a statue destroyed in Temeschwar.
n.Urizen: The Urizen stargazer Valeria of the Cloistered Eye and her spire catalogued the ritual's ripples for the Conclave, Spark planned to visit the Archmage of Night Elyssiathain in the Urizen camp, and Livia of the Spire of the Celestial Cascade was named on the Whisper Gallery's list of Arch-Offenders.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a Kallavesi naga in Hahnmark was reported to have woken to find their hair replaced by red and gold feathers.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is not named; the page only notes heralds of Azoth visiting the Castle of Thorns.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: a Kallavesi naga in Hahnmark reportedly went to sleep with a full head of hair and woke with a covering of brilliant red and gold feathers.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Janon's herald Spark wished to discuss the destruction of a statue in Temeschwar with Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato.

Walk on.d: Each human nation had a contested practice: the Freeborn Feast of the Broken Wheel, Dawnish love and glory, League dead reckoning, Marcher rebirth as non-humans and shriving, the Navarr Great Dance, Urizeni veneration of Sulemaine, Varushkan bargains with sovereigns and Wintermark reverence for ancestors in Kallavesa. Endorsing a nation's mandate would end the fall in its congregations. Highguard was offered a Highborn Assembly mandate committing its people to rooting out blasphemy, idolatry and heresy. The Marcher Assembly could shun the pilgrims or drive off all Highborn with rough music. Dawn could send troubadours to Highguard. All General Assembly mandates except Dawn's passed, and Mael Donjeon of House Remys went to Highguard.

n.Dawn: The General Assembly mandate affirming that love and glory benefit humanity was the only one not enacted, so Dawnish congregations stayed troubled. The Dawn Assembly instead sent Mael Donjeon of House Remys to spread understanding of love and glory in Highguard, despite warnings that this could inflame opinion.
n.Highguard: Highborn pilgrims were the source of the questioning, and Highguard was offered a mandate committing its citizens to eradicating blasphemy, idolatry and heresy, at the cost of narrowing its assembly's focus for a year. It also became the destination of Dawnish troubadours under Mael Donjeon.
n.Navarr: The General Assembly confirmed that nothing in the Great Dance is incompatible with the Way, ending the decline in Navarr congregations. The Navarr Assembly's earlier statement against criticism of hearth magic was noted as irrelevant to the pilgrims' concerns.
n.The Brass Coast: The General Assembly ruled that the Feast of the Broken Wheel, questioned by the pilgrims and by Zemress Islanders, does not diminish doctrine because it is a parody, ending the penalty on Freeborn congregations.
n.The League: The General Assembly declared dead reckoning an embodiment of prosperity rather than a dedication to Vengeance, ending the drop in League congregations.
n.The Marches: The General Assembly ruled that shriving and belief in rebirth as trees or animals do not contradict doctrine, ending the penalty on Marcher congregations. The Marcher Assembly was also offered mandates to shun the pilgrims or drive off all Highborn with rough music, but the page does not record either being enacted.
n.Urizen: The General Assembly held that Sulemaine, though not a recognised paragon, taught Wisdom and is not a false paragon, so Urizeni may call for virtuous humans to be recognised as paragons. This ended the penalty on their congregations.
n.Varushka: The General Assembly confirmed that doctrine no longer forbids bargaining with sovereigns, just as it does not forbid bargaining with eternals, settling whether wise ones and volhov commit idolatry and ending the decline in Varushkan congregations.
n.Wintermark: The General Assembly ruled that 'to sleep in Kallavesa' is a metaphor and that interring heroes in the swamp is like Highborn tombs, ending the penalty on Wintermark congregations.

t.Kallavesa: The practice of interring heroes in Kallavesa's swamps, and the belief that their spirits sleep there, was at the heart of Wintermark's question. The General Assembly declared it a metaphor compatible with the Doctrine of the Labyrinth.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Whittle folk living in Mournwold were cited by Highborn critics as an example of false-virtue followers the Synod tolerates.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Whittle folk living in Tassato were cited by Highborn critics as an example of false-virtue followers the Synod tolerates.

Weight of the world.d: Vasili convinced sceptical locals, used to Druj domination, that the Empire meant to inspire rather than demean them. Two obstacles remained: the miasma and the conviction that the Druj would return. All Imperial armies had left Ossium. The Ketsov suggested a major fortification, or the Empire could permanently station an army or win a sustained defensive campaign. Pillars were located in the Galath Fields and Nearweald, and regions with pillars would be 20% easier for the Druj to conquer. The many orcs of Ossium could not become Varushkan. The Senate could declare them foreigners to work there or escort them to Skarsind. At the Summer Solstice the Senate declared them foreigners.

n.Dawn: Ser Ancél Watcher's Dawn Assembly mandate inspired troubadours and questing knights to scour Ossium's wilderness, and they found the miasma pillars in the Galath Fields and Nearweald.
n.Druj: The Druj are gone from Ossium, but locals are certain they will return and kill anyone who aided the Empire. Their lingering miasma pillars would make affected regions 20% easier for them to retake.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: orcs freed in recent raids on Grendel settlements are cited for comparison, as is the troubled release of former Grendel slaves at Sarvos.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: experience from the Reikos campaign informs the Empire's understanding of the miasma pillars.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Senate could have sent Ossium's orcs to Skarsind, potentially swelling the nation greatly, though it was unclear the Imperial Orcs wanted them. In the end the orcs were declared foreigners, and the Varushkan assembly welcomed Imperial Orc preachers to Ossium.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Ossium's orcs were not deterred from moving to Skarsind by its proximity to the Jotun, an unknown threat they considered far less terrible than the Druj.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League ceded Misericorde in Holberg to the Sand Fishers, and freed Grendel slaves were once left on the docks of Sarvos.
n.Thule: Thule armies in Ossium bring locals little comfort. The Ketsov are nervous of the Thule's reputed thirst for artisans, and the Thule are hoped to deal with the miasma pillar in their own lands.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly welcomed the Ketsov and all of Ossium who would be Varushkan, and Varushkan settlers are arriving. However, the egregore cannot accept orcs, and the locals' fear of the Druj hampers integration.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers were evacuated from Ossium to Misericorde in Holberg, a considerable sacrifice for its inhabitants.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: any overland migration of Ossium's orcs to Skarsind would have to pass through dangerous Karov.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan settlers come to Ossium from Karsk, and any orc migration to Skarsind would have to cross it.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan settlers are coming to Ossium from Miekarova.
t.Ossium: Pride preaching left the people receptive to the Way, but the miasma and fear of the Druj's return, with no Imperial army present, hold back integration. The Senate declared its orcs foreigners, which could let them work for the Ketsov and other Varushkans and speed the territory's growth.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Otkodov have made little attempt to speak with Ossium's people outside the Bonewood.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: veterans of the Reikos campaign remember the miasma, and experience there suggests one pillar per region.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: freed Grendel slaves were once told to head for Skarsind from the docks of Sarvos, which did not end well.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was proposed as a new home for Ossium's orcs, which could have filled the sparsely populated territory to overflowing. The Senate instead declared the orcs foreigners in Ossium.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers were evacuated to Misericorde to fish the Semmerlak and its shores.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Mentioned in passing: the Bittershore's miasma pillar was found and destroyed during the invasion.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Mentioned in passing: the Bonewood is the only part of Ossium where the Thule have spoken with local people.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: Ser Ancél's questers found a Druj miasma pillar in the Galath Fields; until it is destroyed the region would be easier for the Druj to reconquer.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: A Druj miasma pillar was found in the Nearweald; it awaits destruction, and while it stands the region is more vulnerable to Druj conquest.
